differential.name: Platelet activation / possible early myeloproliferative disorder

clinical_reasoning_summary: A 37‑year‑old male presents with severe, untreated stage 2 hypertension (169/105 mmHg) in the setting of obesity, documented untreated obstructive sleep apnea, and early renal impairment (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL). These findings make uncontrolled essential hypertension the most probable primary driver, accounting for the majority of his cardiovascular risk. Untreated OSA acts as a major modifiable contributor, amplifying sympathetic tone and insulin resistance, thereby supporting the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. Early CKD is likely a consequence of chronic pressure overload, while prediabetes reflects the metabolic milieu. Anemia and a markedly elevated platelet distribution width remain unexplained and warrant targeted hematologic work‑up. Secondary endocrine or renovascular hypertension is possible given resistant BP and early CKD, but lacks confirmatory testing at this stage.

recommended_workup: Repeat comprehensive metabolic panel with calculated eGFR
Polysomnography or validated home sleep apnea testing to quantify OSA severity
Plasma aldosterone‑renin ratio with confirmatory suppression testing (screen for primary aldosteronism)
Renal artery duplex ultrasound or CT‑angiography (evaluate for renal‑artery stenosis)
Plasma free metanephrines or 24‑hour urine catecholamines (rule out pheochromocytoma)
Complete blood count with MPV, peripheral smear, iron studies, ferritin, vitamin B12, folate, reticulocyte count (characterize anemia and platelet abnormality)
JAK2 V617F mutation testing if myeloproliferative disorder suspected
Lipid panel repeat in 6‑12 months for trend monitoring
Transthoracic echocardiogram (assess left‑ventricular hypertrophy and cardiac function)
Detailed social‑history interview (tobacco, alcohol, illicit substances, caffeine)
Medication reconciliation including over‑the‑counter and herbal products
Mental health screening and referral to social services for intimate partner violence support
Lifestyle assessment: diet, physical activity, weight‑loss counseling
